name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 3, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m.,
on October 3, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 30, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with the City’s Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.8. Real property Denoted as Assessor’s Parcel No. 784-291-01
  with a Common Street Address of 24701 San Doval, Mission Viejo, California,

City Council Minutes  1  October 3, 2011
   Commonly Known as O’Neill Elementary School Owned by Saddleback Valley
  Unified School District The Negotiating Parties are: City of Mission Viejo; Dennis
  Wilberg, City Manager, Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager, Charles Wilson,
  Director of Community Development, and William Curley, III, City Attorney.
  Owner Negotiators are: Saddleback Valley Unified School District, Clint Harwick,
  Superintendent. Under Negotiation will be the Price and Terms of a Lease-Hold
  Interest in the Real Property.

CS2. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the Council provided
direction to staff for further negotiations on the subject real estate parcel. For item CS2, the
Council gave direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Gene Orr for 35 Years of Service to the Community as Owner of Big O
  To Go Pizza

  Mayor Leckness presented a certificate of commendation to Gene Orr, owner of Big O
  To Go Pizza.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tom McCarthy, M.V.: representing Rancho Mission Viejo Little League, expressed support for
the proposed installation of shade covers at Curtis Park.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: invited Council Members and residents to visit the web site
missionviejobusiness.com which was created to sustain, gain, and retain business in Mission
Viejo. He further commented on redevelopment and stated that Mission Viejo is the poster child
for redevelopment abuse.

City Council Minutes  2  October 3, 2011
 Duane Cave, San Diego Gas and Electric: discussed the September 8, 2011, power outage which
affected 1.4 million customers in San Diego and south Orange County, among other areas. He
noted that it was the first system-wide outage that SDG&E has ever experienced and they are
evaluating what led to the outage and how to prevent future issues of the same kind.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 5, 10, 11, 12, and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Council Member Reardon announced that she pulled items 12 and 13 so that members of the
public could hear answers to the questions that she posed earlier in the day.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 19, 2011, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register dated September 9, 2011 in the amount of $1,756,500.19

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated September 16, 2011 in the amount of $1,680,312.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the Community Development Agency (CDA) -
  Fourth Quarter of 2010-11 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

City Council Minutes  3  October 3, 2011
   Received and filed.

7.  Semi-Annual Financial Reports for the Community Development Financing
  Authority (CDFA) - For the Year Ended June 30, 2011 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Received and filed.

8.  Purchase and Implementation of Computer Network Switches

  (1) Approved a purchase order with Resilient Communications for the purchase of Cisco
  equipment in the amount of $178,983.12; and (2) approved agreement with Resilient
  Communications for purchase of professional services in the amount of $4,000.

9.  Second Amendment to Agreement with AECOM for Professional Services; Time
  Extension Only, No Further Funds

  Authorized the City Manager to Sign the Second Amendment of Agreement with
  AECOM for the Period from August 16, 2011 to August 16, 2013, or as necessary to
  complete all legally required analysis.

14.  Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)-Acquisition of Right-
  of-Way

  Adopted Resolution 11-65 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs
  Related to Capital Improvement Project 791.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

12.  Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Flashing Beacons,
  Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights and CCTV Cameras-Contract
  Extension

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and outlined his
  response to questions that Council Member Reardon posed on items 12 and 13 earlier in
  the day.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Leckness,
  to Approve Sixth Amendment to Contract A07-48 with Republic ITS extending the term
  of the contract to December 31, 2011.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury

City Council Minutes  4  October 3, 2011
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

13.  Montanoso Drive Neighborhood Traffic Management Program, Phase 2 (CIP 779)

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) certify
  the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the
  City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the
  Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance
  and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and
  (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

15.  City of Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (La Paz Channel) 2011
  Special Tax Refunding Bonds

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 11-66 Authorizing Issuance of Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (La
  Paz Channel) 2011 Special Tax Refunding Bonds, and Approving related Documents and
  Actions; (2) adopt CDFA 11-03 Authorizing the Execution and Delivery of an Escrow
  Deposit and Trust Agreement relating to certain 1999 Local Agency Revenue Bonds, and
  Approving related Actions; and (3) approve the selection of Fieldman Rolapp &
  Associates (A11-68) as financial advisor at a cost not to exceed $28,500 including
  expenses, Quint & Thimmig LLP (A11-69) as bond and disclosure counsel at a fee not to
  exceed $55,000, and Stone & Youngberg (A11-70) at a cost not to exceed $9.853 per
  $1,000 of bonds.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  October 3, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

5.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Fourth Quarter of 2010-
  11 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Council Member Schlicht asked what dollar amount should be in each of the replacement
  reserve accounts.

  City Manager Wilberg indicated that staff will supply that information in memo form by
  the end of the week.

  Council Member Kelley shared information on the City’s strong financial position as
  outlined in the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to receive
  and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

10.  Voluntary Alternative Redevelopment Program Ordinance

  Council Member Schlicht indicated that she would vote no on this item because she is
  opposed to any extension of the redevelopment agency. She feels that as the City
  continues to use the RDA, it is basically stealing money from the State and from the
  County.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to adopt
  Ordinance 11-291 Electing to Comply with and Participate in the Voluntary Alternative
  Redevelopment Program Contained in Division 24, Part 1.9 of the California Health and
  Safety Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  October 3, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

11.  Employment Contract for Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, W.
  Keith Rattay

  City Manager Wilberg and City Attorney Curley answered questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 11-XX Approving an Employment Agreement with Mr. W. Keith Rattay.

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury withdrew his motion.

  By consensus, the City Council directed the City Attorney to draft some alternate
  language for Mr. Rattay’s consideration (sections 7 and 8) and return to the City Council
  at a future meeting.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

16.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

17.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA.

18.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

19.  FY 2010-11 General Fund Operating Surplus

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  7  October 3, 2011
   Cliff Swan, M.V.: expressed concern with the proposed site for a dog park and
  recommended that the City Council reconsider the site next to Pavion Park.

  Mayor Leckness read a written comment from resident John Lusk who was also opposed
  to the proposed dog park location near Gilleran Park.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve
  the appropriation of $35,000 to CIP 321 from the General Fund Discretionary Reserves
  for shade covers at Curtis Park Field and the Community Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

20.  One Time Exemption to Municipal Code Chapter 13.04, Sec.13.04.030 (n)
  Prohibiting Individuals From Being in any Park Overnight

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve a one-time exemption to applicable Municipal Code Chapters that prohibit
  individuals from being in any park overnight.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

22.  Appointment of Ad Hoc Committee of the CDA/City Council to Review Proposals
  Received in Response to RFP for Site C

City Council Minutes  8  October 3, 2011
   Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Mayor Leckness appointed Council Members Kelley and Schlicht to the CDA/City
  Council Ad Hoc Committee for the purpose of reviewing proposals for Site C.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Readers’ Festival and she commended
staff and the volunteers who put on another wonderful community event. She noted that it was
well attended and everyone had a great time. Council Member Kelley announced that there will
be a Timeless Melodies music history education program entitled “depression and warriors.”
The event will be presented by Larry Maurer on Sunday, October 16, 2011, at 7:00 p.m. in the
City Council chamber and admission is $10.00. She also reminded residents that the City’s free
Movie of Character “Temple Grandin” will be shown earlier that day beginning at 2:00 p.m.
Council Member Kelley noted that the annual Walk Against Drugs will be held on October 22,
commencing at 8:00 a.m. at Mission Viejo High School with key note speaker Mark Munoz.
From there, participants walk to the Village Green where the City will host a Community Fair
and Disaster Preparedness Expo in partnership with Supervisor Pat Bates. Council Member
Kelley announced that Mission Viejo has been ranked among the best cities in which to live and
has the second best shopping mall in the County, according to the Orange County Register’s 13th
Annual “Best of Orange County” poll. Finally, Council Member Kelley reminded residents that
the Community of Character word for the month of October is respect and she invited those who
are interested in joining the Character Committee to call her or send her an email.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon noted that she too attended the Readers’ Festival and she shared a
funny story about her three grandsons’ antics at the event. She commended the volunteers who
worked at the festival and stated that she had a great time. Council Member Reardon also
discussed her attendance at the Mission Viejo Environmental Association’s annual event where
she learned of their water saving measures and how they have been able to lower association
dues for their homeowners. Council Member Reardon outlined her recent tour of the library and
she thanked Stephanie Tanton and all of the library staff for the informative visit. In addition,
she outlined her attendance at a recent San Onofre Nuclear Generating System (SONGS)
presentation on lessons learned from the Fukushima Dai-ichi Nuclear Power Plant; a League of
California Cities Conference; a “State of the College” breakfast at Saddleback College; and the
grand opening of Delizie Ristorante. Finally, Council Member Reardon reminded residents to
pray for young Cade Spinello who is recovering from a stroke after two brain tumor surgeries.

City Council Minutes  9  October 3, 2011
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she too attended Mission Viejo Environmental
Association’s recent event and she commended the association on its hard work to reduce
association dues for its residents. She noted that all are invited to the grand opening of the
Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce on Wednesday, October 12, 2011, at 6:00 pm. The event
will take place at the Jaguar Land Rover dealership, 28701 Marguerite Parkway, and residents
can RSVP by calling (949) 973-9800. Council Member Schlicht also reminded residents to visit
www.missionviejobusiness.com and she asked the Council to reconsider linking to that site from
the City’s web site. She stated that the site provides wonderful resources and offers a great
introduction to the history of Mission Viejo. Council Member Schlicht expressed enthusiasm for
the Mission Viejo High School Diablos football team which has only lost one game since the
season began. She further outlined her attendance at the Readers’ Festival and the 2011 USA
Cycling Elite National Championships held at the University of Dominguez Hills. Council
Member Schlicht thanked the residents of Mission Viejo for allowing her to represent them and
she concluded her comments by reminding residents that they have the option to delay
installation of smart meters if they are SCE customers.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that he attended the Readers’ Festival and he was impressed
with the number of people attending, even late in the day. Mayor Pro Tem Ury complimented
staff and the volunteers for another great event.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he just completed filming a new City Talk program at the
highest point in Mission Viejo and inside a storm drain along one of the City’s streets. He also
attended the grand opening of the beautiful new Fairhaven Memorial mortuary facility. Mayor
Leckness discussed the Readers’ Festival musical kick-off event with Max Weinberg, renowned
drummer for Bruce Springsteen, former Chicago band-member Bill Champlin, and saxophonist
Mindi Abair. He noted that it was a fantastic evening and he was amazed at the quality of the
artists playing to a packed house in Mission Viejo.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:41 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Dale Herbst, to Monday, October 17,
2011, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  10  October 3, 2011
 __________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 17, 2011

City Council Minutes  11  October 3, 2011
